HVS3 (hereafter, after its catalog ID, US 708)
HVS3 (hereafter, after its catalog ID, US 708) has been classified as a hot subdwarf (SdO/B, Geier et al. 2015) and its most likely origin has been traced back to the galactic disc.
Fig. 16 also shows the inferred ejection velocity of the observed hypervelocity subdwarf US 708, which, including error bars, lies at the upper end of our expected velocity range.

The solid black line and red shading indicate the observed velocity and associated error bars of the hypervelocity hot subdwarf US 708 (Geier et al. 2015). The dashed black line and green areas indicates the galactic escape velocity (Pifl et al. 2014), including error bars.

notes: US 708 and HVS3 are explicitly equated in T:p20-b6. It is included as follow_up: the paper treats it as a previously identified hypervelocity hot subdwarf and compares its inferred velocity with the helium-detonation runaway predictions; T:p20-b0 and I:p20-b0 show US 708 above the Galactic escape velocity.

US 708: US 708 (HVS3) is discussed only as an observed comparison object (T:p20-b6, T:p20-b8; Fig. 16 caption at T:p20-b0). The paper does not state a numerical value or uncertainty for any requested quantity of US 708 in the text; its velocity is only indicated graphically in Fig. 16 (I:p20-b0). No quantities were therefore extracted.
